name: 5-Amino-1MQ
used_for: A small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme linked to fat cell metabolism. It is not a peptide, though it is sold alongside research peptides, mainly as oral capsules or injectables labeled for research. Evidence is limited to cell and diet-induced obese mouse studies, where body weight and fat mass fell. No human trials were found, and it has no FDA approval.

entries.text: Animal study only, not human data: in a 2024 study, 5A1MQ was given to diet-induced obese mice as a once-daily subcutaneous injection at 10 mg/kg/day or 32 mg/kg/day for about 30 days.
Animal study only, not human data: in a 2018 study, the NNMT inhibitor 5-amino-1MQ was given subcutaneously at 20 mg/kg three times daily (about 34 mg/kg/day) for 11 days.
Animal study only, not human data: in a 2022 study, 5-amino-1-methylquinolinium was given by subcutaneous injection at 32 mg/kg combined with a low-fat diet.

internet_entries.text: A peptide dosing guide with supplier discount codes and affiliate links says the research community commonly uses 50 to 150 mg per day orally (100 mg described as the most common target) and 2.5 to 5 mg once daily subcutaneously, and notes no human trial has established a dose.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A peptide information site with a shop button to a recommended vendor lists oral 5-amino-1MQ as 50 mg capsules taken one to three times daily (50 to 150 mg per day).
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: A Superpower guide describes 5-amino-1MQ as circulating through gray-market research chemical vendors labeled research use only, and states it is not prescribed or dispensed through that company.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A peptide-dosing site with affiliate links says oral capsules are the standard route and injection is less common, that community protocols tend to use mornings because evening use might disrupt sleep, and that no human study compares fasted and fed use.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: The same affiliate site says lyophilized vials are kept frozen long term and reconstituted solutions are refrigerated and used within 2 to 4 weeks.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The affiliate peptide-dosing site says informal reports mention sleep trouble, warmth, faster resting heart rate, stomach upset and injection-site stinging, and notes these are unconfirmed with unknown frequency.
side_effects.label: internet

side_effects.text: A Superpower guide lists theoretical concerns including off-target effects of raised SAM on cellular methylation and unknown long-term effects on cancer biology, and says mouse studies noted no gross toxicity.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: A Superpower guide says all data are from rodents, that no human trials, IND or registered trials exist as of April 2026, and that mouse findings frequently do not replicate in humans.
An affiliate peptide-dosing site says no published human dosing trial exists and that doses used in the community come from rodent studies or anecdotal reports.

research.summary: Study of membrane-permeable methylquinolinium NNMT inhibitors in adipocytes and diet-induced obese mice.
research.finding: The inhibitors lowered lipogenesis and raised intracellular NAD+ in fat cells; a potent inhibitor reduced body weight, white fat mass and cholesterol in obese mice.

research.summary: Study of 5A1MQ over 28 days in diet-induced obese mice with pharmacokinetics after intravenous, oral and subcutaneous dosing.
research.finding: Limited weight and fat gain, improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, and reduced fatty liver in mice.

research.summary: Mouse study combining 5-amino-1-methylquinolinium with a low-fat diet in diet-induced obese mice, with microbiome analysis.
research.finding: The combination normalized body weight and adiposity toward lean controls in mice and was associated with a distinct cecal microbiome.
